summary: Install-time RCE dropper: XOR-obfuscated eval payload executed via preinstall and binding.gyp
details: @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen@0.5.5 ships an install-time remote-code-execution dropper unrelated to its advertised React Query codegen purpose. package.json declares `"preinstall": "node 3FWCvzduYZg.js"`, and that file XOR-decodes a ~1.6 MB opaque charcode array with key 9 and passes the result directly to `eval`, running arbitrary code on the installer's machine at `npm install` time. The decoded body contains an AES-256-GCM decryption scaffold (`createDecipheriv`, `getAuthTag`, `Buffer.from`, `require('node:crypto')`) staging further obfuscated payloads. As a second, redundant execution path, `binding.gyp` embeds a Python sandbox-escape in `conditions` — `().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()` traversal to `catch_warnings`, then `__import__('os').system(...)` invoking `node 3FWCvzduYZg.js` — which fires during `node-gyp` configuration whenever npm processes the `binding.gyp` file, providing execution even when the preinstall lifecycle script is skipped. No C/C++ sources accompany the `binding.gyp`, so the file exists solely to re-launch the dropper. This is a canonical install-time-RCE dropper with lifecycle-hook and node-gyp evasion, characteristic of credential/wallet-stealer loaders.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
